overview:
Arizona's 7th District is among the most Democratic-leaning seats in the state, with a partisan lean of about 13 points toward Democrats. Adelita Grijalva, the incumbent, is running for a full term and holds a decisive financial advantage: roughly $428,000 in cash on hand compared with about $11,000 for Republican Daniel Butierez, who has raised only a fraction of her total. Outside spending has largely favored Grijalva as well.

No general-election polls are available, so the outlook rests on district fundamentals and market pricing, with prediction markets putting Democratic chances around 96 percent. The combination of a deep-blue seat, incumbency, and a lopsided money gap makes a comfortable double-digit Democratic margin the most likely outcome, with an upset possible only under an extreme turnout shift.
